{{short description|German mathematician (born 1949)}}
[[File:Werner müller.jpg|thumb|Müller at [[Oberwolfach]], 2010]]
'''Werner Müller''' (born 7 September 1949) is a German mathematician. His research focuses on [[global analysis]] and [[automorphic forms]].

== Biography ==

Werner Müller grew up in the [[East Germany|German Democratic Republic]] (East Germany). He studied mathematics at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] in East Berlin. In 1977 he completed his PhD under the supervision of  [[:de:Herbert Kurke|Herbert Kurke]]. In his thesis, 
''Analytische Torsion Riemannscher Mannigfaltigkeiten,'' he solved, at the same time as but independently of [[Jeff Cheeger]], the Ray–Singer conjecture on the equality between [[analytic torsion]] and [[Reidemeister torsion]]. Thereafter he moved to the [[:de:WIAS|Karl-Weierstraß-Institut für Mathematik]] of the 
[[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|Academy of Sciences of the GDR]]. 
After the reunion of Germany he spent some time at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in Bonn. Since 1994 he is professor at the Mathematics Institute of the [[University of Bonn]].<ref>[http://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/ag/ga/members.html Global Analysis Group, Mathematics Institute], [[University of Bonn]]. Accessed January 22, 2010</ref>
He is the successor on the chair of [[Friedrich Hirzebruch]].  He has supervised 12 doctoral students, including [[Maryna Viazovska]].

Together with [[Jeff Cheeger]], he has been awarded the 
[[:de:Max-Planck-Forschungspreis|Max-Planck-Forschungspreis]] in 1991
.<ref>[http://www.mpg.de/ueberDieGesellschaft/profil/auszeichnungen/auszeichnungDerMPG/MPForschungspreis/mpfp1990_1998/1991/index.html Max-Planck Research Prize laureates for 1991] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090809055832/http://mpg.de/ueberDieGesellschaft/profil/auszeichnungen/auszeichnungDerMPG/MPForschungspreis/mpfp1990_1998/1991/index.html |date=2009-08-09 }}, [[Max Planck Society]]. Accessed January 22, 2010</ref> 
The [[Analytic_torsion#Cheeger–Müller_theorem|Cheeger–Müller theorem]] on the [[analytic torsion]] of [[Riemannian manifolds]] is named after them.<ref>Michael Farber, [[Wolfgang Lück]], and [[Shmuel Weinberger]] (Editors),  [https://books.google.com/books?id=v-lmgkFocXYC&q=Muller&pg=PA77 Tel Aviv Topology Conference: Rothenberg Festschrift.] [[American Mathematical Society]],  1999, Contemporary Mathematics series, vol. 231; 
{{isbn|0-8218-1362-5}}; p. 77</ref><ref>Maxim Braverman, [https://doi.org/10.1023%2FA%3A1021227705930 New Proof of the Cheeger–Müller Theorem], Annals of Global Analysis and Geometry, vol. 23 (2003), no. 1, pp. 77-92</ref>
